findings.problem: QC theoretical_ppm fate is left as an open question (computed-by-formula vs manual input) while defaulting to computed. With QC seed rows lacking dilution inputs, QC theoretical_ppm/recovery_pct stay EMPTY and qc_recovery_low/high stay permanently not-assessable (passed=None) until an analyst hand-enters QC dilutions — a behavior change from the old input-based QC theoretical. It is a decision, not an open question.
findings.fix: State the decision explicitly. Recommended: keep computed-by-formula and add one line to the QC edge case noting the advisory QC-recovery criteria remain not-assessable until QC dilution inputs are entered, so the permanent passed=None is not read as a defect.

findings.problem: User data expresses levels as 1%/5%/... but the seed stores bare integers 1/5/15/... The column is correctly display-only and in no formula, but the display convention (unit:'%') is not stated, risking an implementer reading 1% as 0.01.
findings.fix: Add a note: concentration_pct stores the nominal integer level; the % is a UI display unit, not a 0.01-scale fraction; it is informational and enters no formula.

findings.where: §2c is_standard mask and Edge cases (rename / rows-beyond-seed)
findings.problem: Row membership binds to six exact label strings. A typo'd standard label silently drops that row from the regression and changes every downstream observed_ppm/flux with no surfaced error — a GxP foot-gun. The behavior is documented but buried in edge cases, and nothing asserts the standard count.
findings.fix: Add a self-check assertion that the masked standard count == 6, and promote the rename/added-row behavior to a named 'Known limitation' as a consciously accepted risk.
